rendered:
The premise does not match the document. NFA-F was not the best in capacity retention; it was among the weakest. The paper names NFA-A as the variant with superior retention: it had superior capacity retention (≈80%)[1] after 100 cycles[2] at C/3. The comparison given is NFA 811 (≈70%)[3] and NFA-F (≈50%)[4], so NFA-F retained roughly half its capacity and was the lowest of the variants tested.

The document gives no direct explanation for NFA-F's poorer retention. The authors only offer a hypothesis: we hypothesize that[5] increasing the iron content from 5% to 15%[6] may cause structural transitions that can cause capacity fade[7] during continuous cycling. NFA-F is the composition LiNi0.8Fe0.15Al0.05O2 (NFA-F)[8], so it carries the higher iron content. This is consistent with the voltammetry, where the monoclinic to hexagonal-2 redox couple was depressed in the NFA-F variant[9]. The authors infer that the aluminum-rich composition offers good electrochemical stability[10] and reversibility, and they describe the iron-cycling link as still under investigation.
